sections.h2: What are the choices for selling a house in Bernards Township, NJ?
sections.html:
Bernards Township sellers can list on the open market, sell privately, or take an as-is cash offer. The township adds its own pre-sale steps on top of state rules, so the real schedule depends on how quickly you can clear permits and inspections.

A listing tends to win in a market where the median owner-occupied home is valued at $814,800, because buyers here often use mortgages and expect a full inspection process. Cash fits another set of circumstances: an inherited house in Basking Ridge, a property with unclosed permits, a rental with a tenant moving out, or an owner who needs a firm closing date.

  • List with an agent: highest potential price, longer timeline, repair negotiations after inspection.
  • Private sale: you keep the commission and take on pricing, marketing and the township paperwork.
  • Cash buyer: condition does not hold up the sale, and the offer is discounted for the work the house needs.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about housing in Bernards Township?
sections.html:
Housing values here sit far above the national median of $332,700. The Census Bureau estimates 28,594 residents for July 2025. Owners occupy 83.1 percent of housing units, and the 2020 to 2024 median household income was $194,107, with per capita income at $109,797. Median gross rent was $2,476.

Education levels are high, with 74.2 percent of adults holding a bachelor's degree or higher, and 25.3 percent of residents were born abroad. Children under 18 make up 24.1 percent of the population, and 29.4 percent of residents age 5 and older speak a language other than English at home. Owner costs are steep too: the survey tops out at $4,000 or more per month for owners with a mortgage and $1,500 or more for owners without one.

At these price levels buyers expect a clean permit file, and the township checks for one before any residential sale anyway.

sections.h2: Where is Bernards Township and what is it made of?
sections.html:
Bernards sits at the eastern end of the Somerset Hills and covers 24.33 square miles, nearly all of it land. The Second Watchung Mountain bounds the southwest, the Dead River swamp lies to the south, and the Great Swamp National Wildlife Refuge, the Passaic River and Millington Gorge form the eastern edge. Within the township are Basking Ridge, Liberty Corner, Lyons, Franklin Corners, Mount Horeb, Madisonville and part of The Hills, and the Martinsville ZIP Code 08836 covers a piece of it too.

The area was chartered in 1760 as Bernardston Township and incorporated as Bernards Township on February 21, 1798. Far Hills split off in 1921 and Bernardsville in 1924. Voters turned down a borough of Basking Ridge by better than four to one. The township now has 138.86 miles of roads and neighbors Bedminster, Bernardsville, Bridgewater, Warren, Harding and Long Hill.

sections.h2: What must a Bernards Township seller obtain before closing?
sections.html:
Two things, both issued from 277 South Maple Avenue in Basking Ridge. The first is an inspection and certification of smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and a fire extinguisher from the Bureau of Fire Prevention. The second is a Construction Records Clearance from the Code Enforcement Division. The township's selling guide, revised June 2026, says to create a free account on its online portal to apply.

The clearance rule in the township code says a Construction Records Clearance is required before the sale of any residential structure, and both owner and purchaser can be held responsible if one is not issued. The inspector checks records for open construction or zoning permits, and any open permit must have its final inspection before the clearance issues. File at least 10 business days before the change of ownership. A violation carries a fine up to $1,000, up to 90 days in jail or up to 90 days of community service.

The code exempts several transfers when no one changes occupancy, including title corrections, a transfer between spouses and a transfer by or to an executor or administrator distributing an estate. Mortgage refinancing and home equity loans are exempt as well.

sections.h2: How are Bernards Township property taxes set and paid?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector lists a 2026 total rate of $1.661, made up of $0.275 for the county, $0.030 for county open space, $1.077 for the school district, $0.246 for the municipality and $0.033 for the library. Taxes are due on the first of February, May, August and November, with a 10-day grace period. The township does not accept postmarks as proof of payment, and payment is received only when it is physically in the office.

The Tax Collector collected 99.50 percent of the 2025 levy and handles 10,358 tax accounts and 7,231 sewer accounts as of January 1, 2026. Sewer bills run on a separate cycle, due January 1 and July 1, with a 30-day grace period. If a closing falls in the middle of a quarter, the closing statement prorates the bill, so ask for a current balance for both tax and sewer accounts.

Veteran and senior deductions exist. The senior deduction applies to residents 65 or older as of October 1 of the prior year who live in the home and meet the income limit, so tell your attorney if the seller is receiving one.

sections.h2: Do floods affect a sale in Bernards Township?
sections.html:
They can. The Passaic River runs along the township's edge, and the township keeps a flood information page with flood zone maps for buildings, floodways, open space and township property. It also lists its National Flood Insurance Program Class 7 approval and links to FEMA maps and elevation guides.

Ask a buyer's lender whether the property needs flood insurance, and look up the parcel on the township and FEMA maps before you list. A seller who can show an elevation certificate or a clear zone designation answers a common buyer question in the first week.

sections.h2: What do transit, roads and schools add to Bernards Township listings?
sections.html:
Interstate 78, Interstate 287 and U.S. Route 202 serve the township. NJ Transit's Gladstone Branch stops at Basking Ridge and Lyons stations on the way to Hoboken Terminal, and Lakeland Bus Lines runs a Route 78 rush-hour service from Bedminster to the Port Authority Bus Terminal. Mean travel time to work is 32.5 minutes.

The Bernards Township School District runs six schools, among them Cedar Hill, Liberty Corner, Mount Prospect and Oak Street elementary schools, William Annin Middle School and Ridge High School. Ridge High School won a National Blue Ribbon award in 2009 to 2010. The district reported 4,874 students in 2020 to 2021. Private options include Pingry School's upper campus in Basking Ridge and Saint James School.

sections.h2: What does a cash sale change in Bernards Township?
sections.html:
A cash sale removes the mortgage appraisal and most repair negotiation. It does not remove the Construction Records Clearance, the Bureau of Fire Prevention certification or the state transfer fee, which still attach to the sale. Agree up front on who files each application, because the clearance fee rises as closing nears.

Compare offers on the net amount. A listing in this market may bring a higher price, but it carries commission, staging, inspection credits and holding costs. If a sale price goes above $1,000,000, the buyer owes an extra 1 percent fee on top of the seller's transfer fee.

faqs.q: Does Bernards Township require anything beyond a smoke detector certificate to sell?
faqs.a: Yes. The township also requires a Construction Records Clearance from the Code Enforcement Division before a residential sale. The inspector checks for open construction or zoning permits, which need final inspections before the clearance issues.

faqs.q: How much does a Construction Records Clearance cost in Bernards Township?
faqs.a: $40 when the request comes in more than 10 calendar days before closing, $75 within 10 days and $125 within 4 days. The township asks you to apply at least 10 business days before the change of ownership.

faqs.q: When are Bernards Township property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first of February, May, August and November, with a grace period through the 10th. Payments must be in the Tax Collector's hands by then, since postmarks do not count. Sewer bills are due January 1 and July 1.

faqs.q: Who is exempt from the clearance requirement in Bernards Township?
faqs.a: Certain transfers are exempt if occupancy does not change. They include a deed correction, a transfer between spouses, an executor's or administrator's distribution of an estate, and refinancing or home equity loans.

faqs.q: Does the buyer ever pay a transfer fee in New Jersey?
faqs.a: Only on sales above $1,000,000. The seller pays the standard realty transfer fee in every sale, and the buyer owes an added 1 percent when the consideration exceeds $1,000,000.
